**Visual observations:**
- Corn plants with leaves showing prominent pale/white streaking running parallel to the veins
- Narrow, linear chlorotic streaks along the full length of leaves
- Alternating light and dark green bands following leaf venation
- Multiple leaves heavily affected; plants appear somewhat stunted
- No fungal sporulation, lesions with halos, or dark spots visible

**Reasoning:**
The narrow, continuous white-to-pale-yellow streaks running strictly along leaf veins is the hallmark symptom of **Maize streak virus (MSV)**. This is distinct from:
- Maize dwarf mosaic virus (blotchy mosaic, not linear streaks)
- Maize chlorotic dwarf virus (general chlorosis/yellowing, not streak pattern)
- Gray leaf spot / NCLB (discrete lesions, not streaks)
- Physoderma brown spot (brown spots in midrib zone)

The linear, vein-parallel streak pattern on multiple leaves with no other lesion type is classic MSV.
